summary: Isolate Helm process credentials and network peers and coordinate voluntary disruption
details: Default API and worker to separate pre-provisioned Secrets. Production rejects shared API/worker/migration references and environment Secret imports of another process's authority; development retains explicitly selected legacy fallback behavior.

Enable release/component ingress and egress NetworkPolicies for both daemons and the migration hook. Start with empty application allowlists and narrow configurable DNS peers; require explicit bounded peer-and-port rules for database, storage, signing and configured provider or telemetry traffic.
Create the retained migration policy hook before its account and Job, preserve the prior API policy name for upgrades, and document hook cleanup, additive policy semantics and CNI/propagation limits.

Add release-scoped PodDisruptionBudgets retaining the single API writer and allowing one unavailable worker. Supply a rendered reference network-values example and update canonical operator instructions.

compatibility.notes: Existing Helm installations must provision distinct daemon/migration Secret references and reviewed network values before upgrade. Application traffic is denied by chart policy until explicitly allowed when CNI enforcement is active. Production shared credential references now fail rendering. Disruption budgets may block node drain of the single API writer; coordinate a maintenance outage. Retained migration hook policies require operator cleanup after uninstall or disabling policy, once jobs stop. Explicitly disabling chart policies/budgets requires separately reviewed operational controls.

security: Tests verify process-specific references, selectors, hook ordering, bounded explicit rules and unsafe-value rejection. Secret names do not establish separate credential bytes or IAM grants. NetworkPolicies require an enforcing CNI and combine additively with other matching policies; resource creation order does not prove immediate enforcement. No credentials or cluster settings are changed by this source unit.
limitations: Live cluster admission, CNI allow/deny paths, provider identity and permissions remain operator-owned evidence. Documentation IPs and labels must be replaced before use; dynamic endpoints require controlled egress infrastructure.

Disruption budgets do not provide HA or prevent involuntary failure, explicit scaling/deletion or Deployment rollouts. Required full-ticket migration/deployment/restore/production/final gates and executable runbook qualification remain pending in EVY-1206.
